basis: Congenital platelet and erythroid abnormalities define the disease; cryptorchidism is outside the axes.
Ovarian germ cell tumour; thyroid-type tissue does not establish endocrine dysfunction or thyroid-gland disease.
Intestinal fluke infection directly occupies the intestinal mucosa; ectopic organ infection is uncommon.
Pathological fluid accumulation in brain tissue; underlying causes do not establish additional organ involvement.
Poststreptococcal immune-mediated basal ganglia dysfunction; associated rheumatic carditis is a separate manifestation, not damage caused by chorea.
Radiation injury defines the rectal disease; local vascular and connective-tissue changes belong to the bowel lesion. Sepsis is an occasional separate complication.
Congenital cranial nerve dysinnervation causes abnormal ocular movements; oculomotor synkinesis and ptosis define the phenotype.
Basal cell tumours, odontogenic jaw cysts and characteristic skeletal anomalies define PTCH1-related Gorlin syndrome; falx calcification is non-damaging.
Inherited episodic loss of skeletal muscle strength is the defining phenotype (100%); no evidence establishes nerve involvement or a metabolic disorder.
Embryonal tumour arising in the cerebral hemispheres; no additional organ involvement is established.
